class.name: ChunkedTerrain3D
class.brief_description: Large landscape rendered from a height field, with distance based detail and nearby collision.
class.description:
ChunkedTerrain3D turns a grid of heights into a landscape of any size. The terrain is cut into square chunks of [member chunk_quads] quads. Every chunk has up to [member lod_count] levels of detail, each with half the resolution of the previous one, and the level is picked from the distance between the viewer and the chunk: full detail within [member lod_distance], half detail up to twice that distance, and so on. The number of triangles on screen therefore stays about the same for a 500 m or a 50 km terrain. Short vertical skirts around each chunk hide the cracks that would otherwise open between neighbours of different detail. Heights come from the red channel of [member heightmap] or from an array given to [method set_height_data], for example generated by [FastNoiseLite]. A value of [code]0[/code] is the lowest point and [code]1[/code] the highest; [member height_scale] and [member height_offset] turn them into meters. A 16 bit or floating point image ([constant Image.FORMAT_RH], [constant Image.FORMAT_RF]) keeps full precision; an 8 bit image allows only 256 different heights, which shows as terraces. [codeblock] var noise = FastNoiseLite.new() var dim = 1025 var heights = PackedFloat32Array() heights.resize(dim * dim) for z in dim: for x in dim: heights[z * dim + x] = noise.get_noise_2d(x, z) * 0.5 + 0.5
var terrain = ChunkedTerrain3D.new() terrain.set_height_data(heights, Vector2i(dim, dim)) terrain.size = Vector2(4096, 4096) terrain.height_scale = 400.0 add_child(terrain) [/codeblock] For a large world split into multiple [ChunkedTerrain3D] nodes, optionally call [method set_normal_data] after [method set_height_data]. Sampling one height interval beyond each node's border makes adjacent normals agree across streamed nodes and different LOD levels without increasing pixel shader work. Collision uses [HeightMapShape3D]-style shapes and exists only for chunks within [member collision_distance] of the viewer, so the physics engine never sees the whole landscape. The viewer is the node in [member focus], or the current [Camera3D] when no focus is set. Use [method get_height_at] to place objects on the ground without a physics query. [b]Note:[/b] Scaling the node uniformly works, but non-uniform scale and rotation only affect rendering and the height queries approximately. For a world far from the origin combine the terrain with [FloatingOrigin3D].

method.name: apply_color_patch
method.description: Atomically updates a rectangle of existing vertex colors in sample-grid coordinates. Initialize a complete per-vertex color grid with [method set_color_data] first. Nonfinite RGBA values, wrong lengths, empty or out-of-bounds regions return false without modifying the terrain. Unchanged patches are no-ops. A changed patch invalidates only nearby render meshes while retaining existing heightmap collision shapes, cached LOD errors, and bounds. Rendering meshes are refreshed during the next terrain update, or via [method force_update].

method.name: get_last_region_invalidated_chunks
method.description: Returns the number of cached mesh chunks invalidated by the last height or color region update. Identical patches report zero; this is a locality diagnostic rather than a measured GPU throughput metric.

method.name: apply_height_patch
method.description: Atomically replaces the height samples in [param region] of an existing, script-provided heightfield. [param region] uses source-grid coordinates; the [param heights] array is row-major, containing exactly width × height entries for the rectangle. Every new height must be finite. The patch must lie entirely within the current grid and contain at most 4096 samples. Invalid requests return false and leave the existing terrain unchanged. Identical patches are no-ops. When the values change, only render and collision chunks intersecting the edited samples (plus a one-sample normal-derivative margin) are invalidated. If externally supplied source normals exist, the dirty one-ring normals are recalculated from the edited heights. Bounds and geometric LOD error are recomputed for affected chunks. Rendering meshes and nearby physics collision are refreshed on the normal update cadence; call [method force_update] when immediate synchronous refresh is needed. Unlike [method set_height_data], this does not rebuild the full terrain or discard its color layers and unaffected normal overrides. This is a CPU/main-thread incremental editing API, not GPU mesh-page streaming, threaded collision cooking, or a complete landscape editor.

method.name: bake_horizon_visibility
method.description: Calculates CPU-baked heightfield sky visibility (0 to 1) from eight azimuths, subtracting the local surface slope to avoid darkening a uniformly tilted plane. The output contains one value per input height and can be stored in the blue channel of [method set_color_data]. For seamless borders between independently streamed terrain nodes, pass a height grid padded by at least [param radius_steps] samples on each side, then crop the returned result to the interior. Supply row-major heights matching [param dimensions], positive finite [param spacing] and [param radius_steps] from 2 through 12. Does not allocate textures or add render passes.

method.name: clear_height_data
method.description: Goes back to using [member heightmap] after [method set_height_data] was used.

method.name: force_update
method.description: Rebuilds the terrain if its settings changed and applies the distance based detail and collision selection immediately, instead of at the next [member update_interval].

method.name: get_chunk_count
method.description: Returns the total number of chunks.

method.name: get_chunk_grid_size
method.description: Returns the number of chunks along x and z.

method.name: get_chunk_lod_error
method.description: Returns the cached geometric height deviation for the requested chunk and LOD (0 to 7), in world vertical units. A negative result indicates invalid chunk coordinates or LOD. The value is recalculated for affected chunks after [method apply_height_patch] and [method update_region], so screen-space LOD decisions do not use stale error from before sculpting.

method.name: get_chunk_lod
method.description: Returns the level of detail of the chunk at the given grid position (0 is full detail), or [code]-1[/code] if it has no mesh yet.

method.name: get_collision_chunk_count
method.description: Returns the number of chunks that currently have a collision shape.

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: Returns the world height of the ground below or above [param world_position] (its y is ignored). Outside the terrain the height of the nearest border is returned. The value matches the rendered and the collision surface.

method.name: get_height_data
method.description: Returns the active height samples, row by row.

method.name: get_height_dimensions
method.description: Returns the number of height samples along x and z.

method.name: get_normal_data
method.description: Returns the optional row-major custom vertex normal grid, or an empty array when the terrain computes normals from height data.

method.name: get_normal_at
method.description: Returns the unit surface normal at the x and z of [param world_position].

method.name: get_mesh_streaming_priority
method.description: Returns the uncached mesh streaming priority mode. Zero preserves the original row-major chunk iteration, one schedules new visible meshes near the viewer first, and two also gives a bounded priority bonus to meshes in front of the camera. This mode is used only when [member mesh_build_budget_usec] is positive.

method.name: get_mesh_build_budget_usec
method.description: Returns the opt-in CPU time slice in microseconds for uncached terrain mesh builds. Zero uses immediate mesh generation.

method.name: get_pending_mesh_build_count
method.description: Returns how many required LOD meshes were deferred during the last automatic terrain update. The engine retries these meshes on subsequent frames, without waiting for [member update_interval]. Useful for diagnosing world-streaming hitches.

method.name: get_lod_pixel_error
method.description: Returns the optional maximum terrain simplification error in screen pixels. Zero preserves the original distance-only LOD.

method.name: get_visible_chunk_count
method.description: Returns the number of chunks that are currently drawn.

method.name: is_over_terrain
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the x and z of [param world_position] lie over the terrain.

method.name: set_mesh_streaming_priority
method.description: Changes the ordering of uncached terrain LOD mesh creation within this terrain node. Mode 0 keeps the legacy array order, mode 1 prioritizes the nearest visible chunks that do not yet have a mesh before cached LOD upgrades, and mode 2 adds a modest camera-facing preference (up to 35 percent distance scaling) when a current viewport camera exists. Ties use stable source-grid indices. The actual LOD selection, collision, world generation and materials are unchanged. The property takes effect without rebuilding the terrain.

method.name: set_mesh_build_budget_usec
method.description: Sets the soft per-process-frame mesh generation budget (0 to 20000 microseconds) shared by [ChunkedTerrain3D] instances on the main thread. The first uncached mesh in a frame is always allowed to complete even when it exceeds the budget, guaranteeing progress. Existing visible LOD meshes remain rendered while a replacement is deferred. A value of [code]0[/code] restores the legacy synchronous behavior; [method force_update] bypasses this automatic streaming limit.

method.name: set_lod_pixel_error
method.description: Sets the screen-pixel maximum geometric deviation budget used for automatic heightfield LOD. Positive values use cached deviation measurements per chunk and the active camera's 3D rendering resolution. Small values preserve high relief and mountain outlines; large values reduce triangles on flatter areas. A built-in 10 percent hysteresis limits switches. Updating the value does not regenerate height data, textures or collision. The default of zero preserves the previous distance-only selection.

method.name: set_height_data
method.description: Sets the heights directly, as [code]dimensions.x * dimensions.y[/code] values in rows along x (index [code]z * dimensions.x + x[/code]), normally between [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code]. This replaces [member heightmap] until [method clear_height_data] is called. Refused if the array size does not match or a dimension is smaller than 2.

method.name: set_normal_data
method.description: Supplies normalized source-grid vertex normals, in the same row-major order and dimensions as [method set_height_data]. Normals are validated and normalized on upload, then reused by all terrain mesh LODs, skirts, and [method get_normal_at]. This is useful for eliminating lighting seams between independently streamed terrains: compute border slopes using height samples just beyond each terrain's edge. Empty input restores the built-in finite-difference normals. Updating height data or switching back to a heightmap clears the custom normals; submit them again after [method set_height_data]. This changes lighting only and does not affect collision or height queries.

method.name: update_region
method.description: Invalidates the meshes and nearby collision of chunks touched by [param region], given in source-grid sample coordinates, including one extra sample for vertex normals. Also recalculates their bounds and geometric LOD errors. The invalidation is applied on the next chunk update or with [method force_update]. For direct script-side sample edits, prefer [method apply_height_patch] which validates and commits the data before invalidation.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the terrain casts shadows.
If [code]true[/code], the middle of the terrain is at the node's origin; otherwise its corner with the lowest x and z is.

Number of quads along each side of a chunk. Smaller chunks give finer detail selection and culling but more draw calls; 32 or 64 is a good range. The number of height samples minus one should be a multiple of this value.
Chunks closer than this to the viewer get a collision shape; they lose it again at 25% more distance.
If [code]true[/code], nearby chunks get a static collision shape.
The physics layers the terrain is in.
The physics layers the terrain scans for collisions.

If [code]true[/code], each native GPU terrain chunk is marked as static GI geometry for SDFGI and baked lighting. This flag is applied when streaming new LOD chunks and can be changed for existing chunks without rebuilding their meshes, physics or draw-call batches. For dynamically deforming terrain, disable this property to avoid stale SDFGI lighting. This flag has no additional GI processing cost if SDFGI/lightmaps are disabled.
Node used as the viewer for detail and collision. If empty, the current [Camera3D] of the viewport is used.
Height in meters added to every sample after scaling.
Height in meters of a sample with the value [code]1[/code].
Image whose red channel holds the heights, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Ignored while height data was set with [method set_height_data].
Number of levels of detail. Level 0 is full detail and each further level has half the resolution.

Controls priority within a budgeted terrain node: [code]0[/code] is the original row-major order, [code]1[/code] fills missing visible geometry nearest to the focus before spending time on LOD upgrades, and [code]2[/code] additionally favors chunks in the current camera direction. This is bounded priority, not frustum culling: offscreen chunks will still be generated as time allows. Requires [member mesh_build_budget_usec] greater than zero. A value of zero keeps existing Godot scenes backward-compatible.

Main-thread CPU budget, in microseconds, for newly generated heightfield LOD meshes. When positive, generation is time-sliced over multiple process frames; the current visible LOD remains in use while a new one is built. This is a soft budget, not a hard deadline, because one mesh cannot be interrupted halfway through building. Nodes share the same per-frame clock, so the limit applies to the terrain streamer rather than separately multiplying for every loaded world chunk. The default of zero retains existing Godot scene behavior.
Maximum screen-space geometric deviation in pixels before a terrain chunk switches to a higher-detail mesh. Zero uses the original distance-based algorithm.

Distance within which chunks have full detail. Each further level starts at twice the distance of the previous one. A chunk keeps its level a little past a boundary, so it does not flip back and forth.

Optional weight (0 to 1) of a per-chunk geometric-error-based LOD adjustment. The engine measures the height deviation between the original mesh and a coarser triangulated mesh and caches it once for each visible chunk. Flat areas switch to lower-detail meshes earlier, while rough cliffs and mountain ridges retain silhouette geometry longer. The adjustment is capped and also affects the existing geomorph transition threshold. A value of [code]0[/code] preserves the original distance-only or screen-relative LOD behavior, without computing deviations. Collision, height queries, textures and per-chunk materials are unaffected.

Reference vertical perspective camera field of view in degrees for [member screen_space_lod_enabled]. At 720 pixels of viewport height and this vertical FOV, [member lod_distance] is unchanged. Higher pixel density or a narrower field of view keeps terrain detailed farther away. Ignored by orthographic cameras.
Material of the terrain. Texture coordinates run from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code] over the whole terrain; use a [ShaderMaterial] to splat textures by height or slope.

The visual layers of the terrain chunk instances, matched against [member Camera3D.cull_mask]. Useful to let auxiliary cameras (for example top-down cameras baking a runtime virtual texture) see only the terrain.

If [code]true[/code], rescale distance-based terrain mesh LOD by the internal 3D resolution after viewport scaling and by perspective field of view, inspired by screen-size LOD systems in Unreal Engine and Unity. Dynamic 3D resolution and FSR affect geometry detail because the internal 3D pixel height is used instead of only the output window size. The multiplier is limited to [code]0.6[/code]–[code]1.65[/code]. Disabled by default to preserve existing scenes; cached meshes, collision, skirts, smooth LOD morphing and culling remain unchanged.
Width (x) and depth (z) of the terrain in meters. The distance between samples follows from this and the number of samples.
Depth of the vertical skirts around chunks that hide cracks between different levels of detail. Use at least the height difference one level of detail can produce on your terrain.
Time between two evaluations of detail and collision, in seconds. [code]0[/code] evaluates every frame.
Chunks farther than this from the viewer are not drawn. [code]0[/code] draws the whole terrain.
